newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares rebound to close slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares rebound to close slightly up.

text.p: Jakarta share prices rebounded to record slight gains by the close on Tuesday following late active buying of some big-capitalised stocks and secondaries, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index closed 0.48 points, or 0.08 percent, higher at 567.75 points after touching an intra-day low of 565.36 points. Decliners led advancers by 57 to 51, with 64 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Wednesday as trade was dominated by the upcoming public offer by Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI).
"Corporate news such as acquisitions, rights issues or link-ups with foreign firms could lead to active buying on certain stocks," said one local broker.

But brokers said market sentiment would remain volatile on Wednesday as many investors were concentrating on the BNI offer. BNI is offering about 1.1 billion shares at 850 rupiah per share from November 4, ahead of a November 25 listing on the Jakarta and Surabaya exhanges.
The lead underwriter of the float said preliminary applications for shares in BNI, the country's largest state bank, already total seven times the number of shares on offer.
"It is expected to be heavily oversubscribed as more individual investors are likely to apply during the offer period," an official from the underwriter, PT Danareksa Securitas, said.

Brokers said Tuesday's trading volume was relatively small but active buying on certain stocks including heavyweights Telkom and cigarette maker Sampoerna had pushed the composite index into positive territory.

Telkom rose 25 rupiah to 3,500 rupiah on a volume of about 2.1 million shares following a rise in New York overnight, brokers said. Cigarette firm Sampoerna rose 100 rupiah to 20,950 on a volume of 358,000 shares on good fundamentals, brokers said.

Candy and biscuit producer Mayora Indah topped the active list with 8.2 million shares traded, rising 50 rupiah to 950 rupiah. Brokers said the rise was due to a perception that prevailing prices were low.
Newly listed fisheries company PT Daya Guna Samudra was also actively traded, rising 25 rupiah to 2,150 on a volume of about six million shares after falling to 2,075 rupiah in morning trade.
Brokers ascribed the gains to selective buying after the counter's encouraging debut last week.
